goal:
1. The owner will see one client SDK/provider package that the Ink CLI app and the React frontend app both actually run their episode screens on, replacing today's client SDK, which the owner considers not fully formed.
2. The owner will see every screen in both apps reduced to rendering only, with all data-fetching, subscription and login logic living in the shared provider/hook layer instead of being duplicated inside each app.
3. The owner will see the shared layer give the CLI full tool-card, todo and memory support even though the CLI keeps rendering only the episode surface, with no Telegram-text, email or other module "operational history" view required from it.
4. The owner will see the plan settle on one specific shape — an extended SDK, a set of providers, and one Provider-wrapped app that reaches everything through hooks — in place of the single flat client object with namespaced methods shown in the earlier sketch.
5. The owner will see a clear yes-or-no answer, recorded in the plan, on whether one top-level Provider (not nested per-entity providers) can supply every hook, with each app's own router handing an entity id such as the episode id to hooks like `useEpisode(id)`.
6. The owner will see the hook surface named the way he asked: an `useEpisodeMessaging` hook for sending and stats in place of an `EpisodeScreen`/"episode actions" API, plus separate hooks for episode data, episode context (linked entities), and todos.
7. The owner will see this hook set checked against both apps' real screen layout — a messaging screen with its send line, a context panel, and a separate todo widget — each getting its own hook call through nested components instead of one sequential call site.
8. The owner will see the provider and this agreed hook set delivered so episode screens work end-to-end in both the CLI and the frontend.
9. The owner will see the CLI and frontend made structurally unified wherever the two apps' code can be shared, rather than kept as two separately maintained implementations.
10. The owner will see every new shared behavior confined to the SDK's client package, with any SDK-core addition listed and justified on its own, so no frontend-only code becomes importable from the backend.
11. The owner will see this work built from a branch that has merged the current tip of `origin/staging`, including the already-merged user- and workspace-related stories.
12. The owner will see the frontend's user/workspace authentication flow corrected to match the shared login/session layer, replacing whatever the frontend currently implements incorrectly.
13. The owner will receive one written architecture and interface proposal for the SDK/provider/hook layer to review and approve before any implementation work starts.
14. The owner will see this plan contain no stage-by-stage implementation or test task list, only the architecture and interface decisions, until he approves them.

score.reason: The candidate captures nearly every discussed point but adds substantial elaboration/interpretation beyond what was explicitly stated and lacks concrete numeric or verifiable completion criteria for an executing agent.
